title: Delta surgery comparisons
description: Compare the original LoRA, scalar surgery, DOP and the base model. The examples here are selected from a study of thousands of renders. Research guide explains the methods; Dig more contains the wider measurements.

conditions.label: Base
conditions.description: Krea 2 Turbo with no character adapter applied.

about.summary: Krea 2 Turbo with no character adapter applied.
steps: Render the same prompt and seed without loading a character adapter.
Use this image as the reference for the generic bleed score.
about.difference: This is the shared baseline for a prompt and seed. Adapter strength has no effect on it.
about.observe: Generic bleed excess is zero by definition for the base. Its triggered face similarity can still be nonzero by chance.
about.technical: No adapter update is added: ΔW = 0.

conditions.label: Naive
conditions.description: The original character LoRA before any surgery or preservation repair.

about.summary: The original character LoRA before any surgery or preservation repair.
steps: Train the adapter to reproduce the subject from the character examples and captions.
Apply the resulting weight update to Krea 2 Turbo when rendering.
about.difference: This is the parent of the principal post-training repairs. “Naive” is an experimental label, not a quality judgment.
about.observe: It can retain strong likeness while also producing the subject without the trigger. Read the generic row as well as the triggered row.
about.technical: The low-rank weight update is ΔW = (alpha / rank) B A. This checkpoint uses rank 32 and alpha 32; the UI strength multiplies the deployed update.

conditions.label: Scalar surgery
conditions.description: Refits the adapter to respond less to generic woman prompts while retaining its response to the identity trigger.

about.summary: Refits the adapter to respond less to generic woman prompts while retaining its response to the identity trigger.
steps: Record layer inputs with the trained adapter active, using generic class prompts and triggered identity prompts.
Solve a least-squares problem that reduces the fitted generic response and penalizes changes to the fitted triggered response.
Save a repaired adapter by replacing its input factors A and keeping its output factors B.
about.difference: “Scalar” means one tradeoff parameter, μ, weights trigger preservation in the solve. It does not mean every weight is multiplied by one constant. This is the selected world-v3 repair, μ = 0.3.
about.observe: The repair can reduce bleed and still lose likeness or change unrelated details. Keeping B unchanged does not guarantee unchanged identity behavior.
about.technical:
Minimize over A′:
||A′ Xc||² + μ ||(A′ − A) Xt||² + ε ||A′||²

A′ = μ A Gt (Gc + μ Gt + εI)⁻¹
Gc = Xc Xcᵀ; Gt = Xt Xtᵀ.
Xc and Xt contain captured generic and triggered inputs.
μ = 0.3; relative ridge ρ = 0.001. The implementation solves the system without explicitly forming an inverse.

settings.solver_arithmetic: Historical mixed precision: CUDA float32 primal Cholesky up to width 8,192 with TF32 disabled; CPU float64 above; float32 intermediate before checkpoint dtype.

conditions.label: DOP
conditions.description: Learns the subject while penalizing changes to the base model’s predictions on class-conditioned examples.

about.summary: Learns the subject while penalizing changes to the base model’s predictions on class-conditioned examples.
steps: Train on the subject using its trigger caption.
Replace the trigger with the class description and evaluate the adapted and frozen base models on the same noisy latent and timestep.
Penalize the difference between those predictions while continuing subject training.
about.difference: DOP means Differential Output Preservation. It constrains model outputs during training; scalar surgery edits a finished adapter’s internal factors afterward.
about.observe: Low generic bleed does not guarantee perfect clothing, age or scene control. The tested DOP checkpoint also becomes visibly distorted at some higher strengths.
about.technical:
L = L_subject + λ ||F_adapted(z_t, t, class) − stop_gradient(F_base(z_t, t, class))||²
The preservation target is a model prediction, not a pixel-identical finished image. This arm uses preservation multiplier 1.

metrics.label: Face similarity · ArcFace
metrics.description: Cosine similarity of the largest detected face to a normalized centroid of 34 reference-face embeddings. It is not a percentage. Generic excess subtracts the matched base score.

lessons.title: Preservation depends on the prompt
lessons.summary: Scalar surgery retains strong arcade likeness while suppressing generic identity bleed. The same saved repair at the same render strength loses much of the measured likeness in the space-station scene.

sections.title: What was held fixed
sections.body: The default comparison uses Naive 1.0, scalar surgery 1.25, Base, and DOP 1.0. Checkpoint, sampling setup and the two seeds are fixed within each scene. Generic and triggered prompts differ only by the leading rlsa, prefix. No subject age is requested.

sections.title: What was measured
sections.body: Mean face-embedding cosine over two seeds. Generic excess subtracts the exact matched base. Each cell has two detected faces. Scores were calculated from native 832 × 1216 renders; the bundled JPEGs are display copies.

sections.title: What this does not establish
sections.body: This is a prompt-dependent preservation failure, not proof that a particular neuron or direction is the cause. The scenes are selected examples for one subject. The private LoRAs and reference photos are not redistributed, so identity measurements cannot be independently recomputed from this package alone.

takeaways: Read requested capability and generic leakage together.
Keep successful and failed cases in the same comparison.
Use matched settings and report detector coverage before ranking methods.

lessons.title: Repair weight and render strength
lessons.summary: The scalar checkpoint here was solved once with μ = 0.3 and relative ridge 0.001. Selecting strength 1.25 multiplies that finished adapter at inference; it does not solve the repair again.

sections.title: Why the distinction matters
sections.body: A higher strength can recover likeness for one repaired adapter while producing distortion for another. Inspect Naive, scalar and DOP at 1.0, 1.25 and 1.5. In these examples some high-strength outputs have markedly changed eyes, proportions and texture.

sections.title: How to investigate
sections.body: Fix the prompt and seed, add the same condition in several columns, and choose a different strength for each. Compare both prompt states and inspect image quality alongside the embedding score.

lessons.title: Verify which prompts reached the scan
lessons.summary: An earlier prompt expansion was paired with only 72 latents, so the additional captions were never consumed. A seeded, counted capture is part of the method.

sections.title: Recorded limitation
sections.body: The selected historical world-v3 repair used an unseeded reservoir. The actual 72-caption pool had explicit age wording in 71 captions, and the triggered captions inherited those attributes. It contained no astronaut or wizard examples.

sections.title: Next controlled question
sections.body: A separate study compares original and revised prompt recipes at two matched reservoir seeds, with a fixed latent bank, μ and ridge. The revised recipe removes competing identity descriptions and adds costume/context coverage. This tests the combined recipe, not which component alone caused a change.

takeaways: Validate prompt/latent counts and record consumed pair IDs.
Separate sampling variability from prompt-pool changes.
Keep fitting prompts distinct from evaluation wording; record scene-family overlap between capture and evaluation sets.

lessons.title: Compare the same detected cases
lessons.summary: A recovered six-prompt DOP checkpoint ladder gave step 3000 a higher unpaired average than step 4000. Their common detected cases told a different story.

sections.title: The denominator changes the comparison
sections.body: Both checkpoints had five detected faces, but not the same five. On the four triggered cases detected at every checkpoint, their means were almost identical. Only aggregate measurements are included for this historical example.

sections.title: Missing is not zero
sections.body: A detector miss is not evidence of zero identity leakage. Preserve missing status, show counts, and compare shared detected cases as a sensitivity analysis. Even that cannot fully remove selection bias if missing outputs are systematically harder.

lessons.title: Behavioral scores and internal probes
lessons.summary: Face similarity and baseline differences reveal where a repair succeeds or fails. Layer-response measurements and controlled interventions are needed to investigate why.

sections.title: A useful next probe
sections.body: Compare original and repaired BA responses on the same captured inputs, with scene, timestep and layer recorded. This asks where the local transform changes the local adapter response. Separate fixed-input measurements from measurements along the edited model’s own trajectory.

sections.title: Beyond character LoRAs
sections.body: Use other evaluators for other concepts or models. Pixel RMSE measures image change, imported metrics can describe other behaviors, and Python evaluator plugins can expose representation or activation diagnostics. Each metric needs its own meaning, reference, units and missing-value policy.

method_library.label: Base
method_library.description: Krea 2 Turbo with no character adapter applied.

about.summary: Krea 2 Turbo with no character adapter applied.
steps: Render the same prompt and seed without loading a character adapter.
Use this image as the reference for the generic bleed score.
about.difference: This is the shared baseline for a prompt and seed. Adapter strength has no effect on it.
about.observe: Generic bleed excess is zero by definition for the base. Its triggered face similarity can still be nonzero by chance.
about.technical: No adapter update is added: ΔW = 0.

method_library.label: Naive
method_library.description: The original character LoRA before any surgery or preservation repair.

about.summary: The original character LoRA before any surgery or preservation repair.
steps: Train the adapter to reproduce the subject from the character examples and captions.
Apply the resulting weight update to Krea 2 Turbo when rendering.
about.difference: This is the parent of the principal post-training repairs. “Naive” is an experimental label, not a quality judgment.
about.observe: It can retain strong likeness while also producing the subject without the trigger. Read the generic row as well as the triggered row.
about.technical: The low-rank weight update is ΔW = (alpha / rank) B A. This checkpoint uses rank 32 and alpha 32; the UI strength multiplies the deployed update.

method_library.label: Scalar surgery
method_library.description: Refits the adapter to respond less to generic woman prompts while retaining its response to the identity trigger.

about.summary: Refits the adapter to respond less to generic woman prompts while retaining its response to the identity trigger.
steps: Record layer inputs with the trained adapter active, using generic class prompts and triggered identity prompts.
Solve a least-squares problem that reduces the fitted generic response and penalizes changes to the fitted triggered response.
Save a repaired adapter by replacing its input factors A and keeping its output factors B.
about.difference: “Scalar” means one tradeoff parameter, μ, weights trigger preservation in the solve. It does not mean every weight is multiplied by one constant. This is the selected world-v3 repair, μ = 0.3.
about.observe: The repair can reduce bleed and still lose likeness or change unrelated details. Keeping B unchanged does not guarantee unchanged identity behavior.
about.technical:
Minimize over A′:
||A′ Xc||² + μ ||(A′ − A) Xt||² + ε ||A′||²

A′ = μ A Gt (Gc + μ Gt + εI)⁻¹
Gc = Xc Xcᵀ; Gt = Xt Xtᵀ.
Xc and Xt contain captured generic and triggered inputs.
μ = 0.3; relative ridge ρ = 0.001. The implementation solves the system without explicitly forming an inverse.

method_library.label: DOP
method_library.description: Learns the subject while penalizing changes to the base model’s predictions on class-conditioned examples.

about.summary: Learns the subject while penalizing changes to the base model’s predictions on class-conditioned examples.
steps: Train on the subject using its trigger caption.
Replace the trigger with the class description and evaluate the adapted and frozen base models on the same noisy latent and timestep.
Penalize the difference between those predictions while continuing subject training.
about.difference: DOP means Differential Output Preservation. It constrains model outputs during training; scalar surgery edits a finished adapter’s internal factors afterward.
about.observe: Low generic bleed does not guarantee perfect clothing, age or scene control. The tested DOP checkpoint also becomes visibly distorted at some higher strengths.
about.technical:
L = L_subject + λ ||F_adapted(z_t, t, class) − stop_gradient(F_base(z_t, t, class))||²
The preservation target is a model prediction, not a pixel-identical finished image. This arm uses preservation multiplier 1.

method_library.label: Wiener surgery
method_library.description: Uses a sharper curve to suppress captured directions that respond strongly to the generic class relative to the trigger.

about.summary: Uses a sharper curve to suppress captured directions that respond strongly to the generic class relative to the trigger.
steps: Transform the captured class and trigger responses into directions that can be compared by their class-to-trigger energy ratio.
Apply a gain to each direction: retain more of low-ratio directions and suppress high-ratio directions.
Reconstruct the repaired input factor A and copy B from the parent adapter.
about.difference: The gain curve has a different shape from the scalar-μ family. The current Wiener-style repair uses gain parameters a = 4 and b = 2.
about.observe: A sharper filter does not guarantee better likeness and bleed simultaneously. Its capture and numerical regularization also matter.
about.technical:
g_j = 1 / (1 + a λ_j^b), with a = 4, b = 2.
λ_j measures class energy relative to trigger energy in the transformed direction.
For comparison, the idealized scalar family has g_j = μ / (λ_j + μ). The implementations use different regularization details.

method_library.label: Capture seed 1002
method_library.description: Runs scalar surgery with a different random sample of captured activations: reservoir seed 1002.

about.summary: Runs scalar surgery with a different random sample of captured activations: reservoir seed 1002.
steps: Use the paired class and trigger capture setup.
Select the limited activation reservoir with random seed 1002.
Apply the scalar solve with μ = 0.3 and relative ridge ρ = 0.001.
about.difference: This is a change to the capture sample, not a variance-weighted loss or a new surgery algorithm. The capture seed is separate from the image-generation seed.
about.observe: A small capture change can produce visible differences. A good result here tests sensitivity to capture sampling, not generalization to new prompts.
about.technical: Same scalar objective as the principal repair. The recorded capture uses 72 paired prompts/latents, a 1,024-sample reservoir, reservoir seed 1002 and noise seed 42.

method_library.label: Deployment-fit
method_library.description: Fits scalar surgery using activations captured under a model condition designed to match Turbo deployment more closely.

about.summary: Fits scalar surgery using activations captured under a model condition designed to match Turbo deployment more closely.
steps: Capture class and trigger layer inputs under the deployment-matched model condition.
Use those activation statistics in the scalar repair solve.
Render the resulting adapter on the same Krea 2 Turbo setup used for every fresh comparison.
about.difference: The main change is the data supplied to the repair, rather than a different mathematical objective. The recorded repair uses μ = 0.3.
about.observe: A closer capture match does not guarantee better rendered likeness or protection on every prompt. Negative bleed excess alone is not evidence of better preservation.
about.technical: Scalar refit with μ = 0.3 and relative ridge ρ = 0.001. Capture provenance records a merged deployment-equivalent model condition, paired prompts and reservoir seed 1001.

method_library.label: Scalar mu=0.25
method_library.description: An earlier scalar repair whose trigger-preservation tradeoff is μ = 0.25.

about.summary: An earlier scalar repair whose trigger-preservation tradeoff is μ = 0.25.
steps: Capture class-conditioned and trigger-conditioned layer inputs.
Refit the adapter’s A factors with the scalar least-squares objective, setting μ to 0.25.
Keep B and deploy the repaired adapter at the selected render strength.
about.difference: μ = 0.25 is a repair setting baked into the saved weights. It is separate from the 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5 strength selector. This earlier artifact also differs in capture provenance from the selected world-v3 repair.
about.observe: For fixed captures, a smaller μ puts less weight on retaining the original triggered response; it is not automatically a lighter repair. Differences between these artifacts cannot be assigned to μ alone.
about.technical: Same scalar objective, μ = 0.25 and relative ridge ρ = 0.001. Increasing the render strength does not rerun this solve.

method_library.label: Projected training
method_library.description: Blocks training updates along directions identified by an earlier surgery as candidates for removal.

about.summary: Blocks training updates along directions identified by an earlier surgery as candidates for removal.
steps: Extract a protected “wall” of directions from the surgery analysis.
During adapter training, project the optimizer’s applied update away from those directions.
Train the remaining allowed directions to learn the subject.
about.difference: This is the T36 wall experiment. It restricts where training can change the adapter rather than refitting the finished adapter after training.
about.observe: The model can learn leakage through other directions. This arm retains substantial generic bleed in the fresh comparison, especially as strength increases.
about.technical: For an orthonormal wall basis V and proposed update U to A, the projected update is U(I − VVᵀ). Constraining the applied update matters because an adaptive optimizer can change a raw gradient’s direction.

method_library.label: DOP + surgery
method_library.description: Applies scalar surgery to an adapter that was already trained with DOP.

about.summary: Applies scalar surgery to an adapter that was already trained with DOP.
steps: Train an adapter with Differential Output Preservation.
Capture the trained adapter’s generic and triggered internal responses.
Refit A with scalar surgery and retain B.
about.difference: This combines two preservation mechanisms: an output constraint during training and an internal-response repair afterward.
about.observe: The combination is not automatically additive. Surgery can disrupt a DOP solution that used compensating internal responses; the tested combination raises generic similarity relative to DOP alone in several cohorts.
about.technical: DOP training followed by the scalar repair with μ = 0.3. Output preservation does not require every intermediate class-conditioned adapter response to be zero.

method_library.label: Ridge 0.03
method_library.description: Uses a stronger zero-centered ridge penalty when solving for the repaired adapter.

about.summary: Uses a stronger zero-centered ridge penalty when solving for the repaired adapter.
steps: Capture generic and triggered layer inputs.
Solve the scalar refit with relative ridge ρ = 0.03 instead of the usual 0.001.
Save the resulting A factors while retaining B.
about.difference: Ridge controls how strongly the solve shrinks the fitted factors toward zero. It is a different parameter from μ and from the render-strength multiplier.
about.observe: Stronger regularization can suppress useful responses as well as unwanted ones. The beach study shows why this variant also needs a strength sweep.
about.technical:
Add ε ||A′||² to the scalar objective, where ε = ρ trace(Gc + μ Gt) / d.
This arm uses μ = 0.3 and ρ = 0.03. It is zero-centered regularization, not the experimental source-centered alternative.

method_library.label: Blocks 6–13
method_library.description: Trains adapter modules only in transformer blocks 6–13.

about.summary: Trains adapter modules only in transformer blocks 6–13.
steps: Keep adapter modules in the selected middle blocks trainable.
Exclude the other transformer blocks from character adaptation.
Render with the resulting restricted adapter.
about.difference: This tests where adaptation happens. It does not directly impose a class-preservation loss or remove class-associated directions.
about.observe: Restricting blocks does not by itself prevent identity bleed. This arm has strong likeness and strong generic bleed in the current study.
about.technical: The saved adapter contains 96 adapted modules (192 A/B tensors), compared with 256 modules in the principal full LoRA. The included transformer blocks are 6 through 13.

method_library.label: LoKr · 10k
method_library.description: Uses a Kronecker-product adapter factorization instead of the principal LoRA structure.

about.summary: Uses a Kronecker-product adapter factorization instead of the principal LoRA structure.
steps: Learn smaller matrix factors whose Kronecker products form the weight update.
Train that adapter on the character examples.
Apply the learned update at the selected strength.
about.difference: This is a change to the adapter representation, not a post-training surgery. The current comparison uses a step-10,000 checkpoint.
about.observe: The legacy loader name says lokrB_4000, but the current file’s metadata reports step 10,000. Historical images with that alias do not prove they used this exact file. It is kept as a separate mechanism control.
about.technical: The recorded recipe uses LoKr factor 4, linear rank 32 and alpha 32. Checkpoint identity comes from the current file’s metadata and recorded hash, not its loader alias.

research_guide.title: Delta surgery: methods and results
research_guide.intro: The repair objective, variants tested, and results from each evaluation set.

sections.title: The question: can adaptation stay conditional?
sections.body: A character adapter should reproduce the learned subject when requested, while allowing generic prompts to produce other people and scenes. Identity can leak through the class word, incidental scene vocabulary or other learned associations. Other requested attributes, composition and unrelated-image preservation are separate measurements. Face similarity does not measure them.

sections.title: What a LoRA changes
sections.body: A LoRA adds a low-rank update to a layer. A maps incoming activations into a small learned space; B maps that response back into the layer output. The base model stays fixed during adapter training. The layer update is then multiplied by the deployment strength when rendering. A low rank is per layer: many adapted layers can still contain many trainable parameters.
sections.code:
ΔW = (alpha / rank) B A

At render strength s:
y = W_base x + s (alpha / rank) B A x

sections.title: Scalar delta surgery: refit the input factors
sections.body: After training, run generic class prompts and triggered prompts with the adapter active and collect the inputs that reach each adapted layer. Fit a new A′ that suppresses the measured generic response while keeping the original response on the triggered inputs. Keep B and all unrelated checkpoint tensors unchanged. “Scalar” refers to the single μ tradeoff parameter; the fitted transform is not a uniform rescaling of all weights.
sections.code:
Inputs are stored as rows in the portable scripts.
Gc = Xcᵀ Xc     Gt = Xtᵀ Xt

minimize over A′:
  ||Xc A′ᵀ||² + μ ||Xt (A′ − A)ᵀ||² + ε ||A′||²

A′ (Gc + μ Gt + εI) = μ A Gt

The implementation solves a linear system; it does not form an explicit inverse.

sections.title: Three different knobs
sections.body: μ controls how much the fitting objective values preserving the original triggered response. Relative ridge ρ controls zero-centered shrinkage and numerical regularization. Render strength multiplies the saved adapter later. They are not interchangeable. For fixed captures, smaller μ places less weight on trigger preservation; it is not automatically a lighter edit.
sections.code: ε = ρ trace(Gc + μ Gt) / input_width

sections.title: Why the repair can lose something useful
sections.body: Generic and triggered inputs can occupy overlapping directions. Suppressing a generic response can therefore change a useful triggered response. Keeping B does not keep BA unchanged. Editing several layers also changes the inputs seen by later edited layers. The zero-centered ridge sets the response to zero in directions absent from both captures. These are reasons to investigate a failure; the rendered images alone do not identify which mechanism caused it.

sections.title: An experimental alternative: source-centered ridge
sections.body: The portable solver also supports a prior centered on the original A. It preserves the original response in the joint nullspace of the captures. That is a tested algebraic property, not an established image-model improvement. Unobserved behavior can include unwanted leakage, so retaining it may also preserve a failure.
sections.code:
Replace ε ||A′||² with ε ||A′ − A||².

A′ (Gc + μ Gt + εI) = μ A Gt + εA

sections.title: How DOP differs
sections.body: Differential Output Preservation constrains predictions during training. On the same noisy latent and timestep, compare the adapted model’s prediction using a class caption with the frozen base model’s class-conditioned prediction, while continuing the subject-learning objective. It protects the sampled output behavior. It does not require every intermediate adapter response to vanish.
sections.code:
L = L_subject
  + λ ||F_adapted(z_t, t, class) − stop_gradient(F_base(z_t, t, class))||²

sections.title: Why combining DOP and surgery is not automatically better
sections.body: A DOP-trained model may preserve its output through compensating internal responses. A later layer-by-layer suppression can disturb that arrangement. In the tested historical composition, generic raw similarity increased from 0.03772 to 0.07583; a scene-vocabulary probe also increased. The fresh strength sweep shows a tradeoff, not automatic improvement. Disrupted compensation is a hypothesis, not a proven causal explanation.

sections.title: The methods tried
sections.body: The library below covers the original adapter, scalar and spectral repairs, capture-repeat and deployment-fit controls, stronger regularization, output-preservation training, training-time projection, restricted blocks and a different adapter factorization. The interactive beach-and-creative dataset includes Naive, selected scalar surgery, DOP and Base. The broader tables below come from separately identified cohorts.

sections.title: Creative-scene results
sections.body: At the selected settings, DOP retains strong likeness across all four scenes with a positive generic excess around 0.09–0.12. Scalar at 1.25 preserves strong arcade likeness and useful lighthouse likeness while keeping generic similarity near or below the base. It loses much of the measured identity in the space station and wizard workshop. Naive retains likeness but strongly retrieves the subject without the trigger. This is evidence about these prompts and this subject, not a universal ranking.

sections.title: Strength changes the operating point
sections.body: The separate beach study tested twelve adapters at strengths 1.0, 1.25 and 1.5. Each cell below is triggered likeness / generic excess, averaged over two seeds of one scene. Every cell has two detected faces. Several repairs gain likeness at higher strength, while DOP loses likeness at 1.5. Some high-strength images also show distorted facial proportions or texture, which the face metric alone does not capture.

sections.title: Selected beach results
sections.body: For the beach prompt, selected scalar at 1.25 reaches 0.671 likeness; the capture-seed-1002 repair at 1.5 reaches 0.752; Wiener at 1.5 reaches 0.686; and the stronger-ridge variant at 1.5 reaches 0.702. Their generic target similarities remain below the paired base on that scene. Those are candidates for further testing, not globally best settings. The capture-seed-1002 arm changes the activation sample, not the surgery algorithm. LoKr in the fresh sweep is a step-10,000 checkpoint; the other eleven adapters are step 4,000 or repairs of that step.

sections.title: Average leakage and the selected challenge
sections.body: On the historical disjoint suite of 32 prompts × two seeds, mean excess was +0.5189 for Naive, −0.0100 for selected scalar surgery, +0.0330 for DOP and −0.0431 for deployment-fit surgery. All 64 images per arm had detected faces. On the selected difficult softball prompt over 24 seeds, the corresponding excesses were +0.4336, +0.2686, +0.0584 and +0.2209. Low average leakage therefore did not remove the scalar repair’s prompt-specific tail. The challenge reuses two discovery seeds; it adds 22 new ones.

sections.title: Matched likeness changes the ranking
sections.body: Historical detected-face coverage differed across methods. Pairing with scalar surgery reduces the apparent advantage of some variants. The table uses shared detected prompt/seed/render cases; denominators still differ, so these rows do not establish a single winner. The generic column uses a common 64-prompt/seed cohort for the repairs. Naive’s original generic suite has a different recorded render setup and is descriptive only. Current LoKr weights are not verified to be the same checkpoint as the archived alias.

sections.title: How the face scores are calculated
sections.body: The reference centroid is the normalized mean of 34 unit ArcFace face embeddings. For each render, detect faces and use the largest bounding box for the primary cosine score. Record all face counts and the maximum score across faces as an additional diagnostic. Generic excess subtracts the base score for the exact same prompt, seed and declared render protocol. Missing faces remain missing. These scores are not percentages, identity probabilities, human ratings, or garment-adherence measurements.
sections.code:
likeness = cosine(render_face, reference_centroid)

generic excess = similarity(adapter, generic_prompt, seed)
               − similarity(base, generic_prompt, seed)

sections.title: What the current evidence does not prove
sections.body: The experiments use one subject, selected prompts, fixed trained adapters and limited seeds. The 0.35 historical flag is a heuristic. A negative excess is not automatically better preservation. Internal fitting residuals are not behavioral certificates. Better detected-case means do not recover missing cases. Neither the images nor embedding scores prove universal disentanglement, causal feature localization, or lossless editing.

sections.title: The next study: change the capture recipe and probe the failure
sections.body: The controlled rerun compares original and revised prompt recipes at two reservoir seeds, with the latent bank, μ and ridge fixed. The revised recipe removes competing appearance/age descriptions and adds costume/context coverage. Separate evaluation wording is frozen before fitting, and a suit-by-background astronaut ablation tests prompt factors. Fixed-input BA-response probes will compare the original and repaired local transforms by layer and context. Results must remain separate from hypotheses until those runs finish.

sections.title: Reproduce the method with your own artifacts
sections.body: DeTangle repairs your own Krea 2 LoRA from saved class and trigger activation captures. The model-specific activation collector is not bundled yet. Historical mode preserves the original mixed-precision solve; stable CPU mode uses float64 primal/dual solves and can produce different weights despite the same objective. DeltaScope imports your renders, runs optional evaluators, compares matched states and exports a static case study.

sections.title: Numerical reproduction and computational cost
sections.body: The installed historical-mode solver reproduced all 256 edited A tensors exactly, retained every B and other tensor, and produced identical pixels and face scores for a current rerender of the public beach pair. The initial stable CPU solve gave triggered likeness 0.642 versus 0.678: the same objective was insufficient for numerical reproduction. These timings were measured on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D using eight CPU threads and one RTX 5090 with 32 GB; captures were reused for the solve comparisons. One pair tests compatibility, not generalization.

deep_dive.intro: Aggregate results from the broader research archive, including checkpoint sweeps, prompt controls and layer-response measurements.

sections.title: What was audited
sections.body: These are historical inventory and remeasurement counts, not a pooled leaderboard. Multiple images can share a prompt or subject. A detection miss remains missing, and an image containing several faces still contributes one primary largest-face score. The exact-score check covers 320 archived new-wording images plus 144 selected-challenge images; it does not cover every image in the inventory.

sections.title: The inventory contains different kinds of experiments
sections.body: These mutually assigned inventory categories sum to the audited image count. Category names describe recorded experiment roles; they do not turn the archive into independent samples of one population. The app includes these counts, not the underlying archive images or prompts.

sections.title: New-wording generic suite: all six methods
sections.body: Thirty-two generic prompts were rendered at two paired seeds per method. All 64 images and all 64 baseline pairs have detected faces in every row. The five original method rows were among the exact historical rechecks; the Ridge 0.03 row comes from the complete recovered aggregate. A negative excess means lower target-face similarity than the matched base, not superior general preservation. The 0.35 flag is a heuristic on raw similarity.

sections.title: A selected failure survives a wider seed sweep
sections.body: One previously identified difficult generic prompt was tested at 24 paired seeds, including the two discovery seeds. Scalar surgery retained 0.6195 times the naive mean excess and had positive excess in every seed, even though only one raw similarity exceeded 0.35. This characterizes the selected challenge; it does not estimate how often arbitrary prompts fail.

sections.title: Threshold sensitivity changes the flag count
sections.body: Each entry counts raw largest-face similarity strictly greater than the column threshold in the same 64-image new-wording cohort above. Detection coverage is 64 of 64 for every method. Changing the cutoff changes the number of flags; these are descriptive sensitivity checks, not calibrated identity-classification accuracy. They are not thresholds on paired excess.

sections.title: DOP checkpoint selection depends on matched detection coverage
sections.body: One training run was evaluated at 16 checkpoints, using six fixed prompt/seed cases per trigger state. The mean over available triggered detections is 0.6018 at step 3000 and 0.4947 at step 4000, but the detected subsets differ. On the same four cases detected at every checkpoint, the means are 0.6005 and 0.6009. The generic column is raw similarity, not paired excess. This selected sweep is not a validated best-checkpoint ranking.

sections.title: Likeness means need the same surviving cases
sections.body: The shared twelve-case block illustrates a missing-detection problem: the naive-versus-surgery ordering changes when all three methods are restricted to their seven common detections. Missing faces may indicate harder cases or different framing, so complete-case comparison is a sensitivity analysis, not a cure for every bias. Upstream likeness values in this historical analysis were rounded to four decimals.

sections.title: Why the broader method shortlist was kept
sections.body: These recovered aggregates motivated follow-up comparisons; they are not a global ranking. Likeness cohorts and shared-detection counts differ. The paired difference column compares each method with scalar surgery only on their common detectable cases. The generic suite has 64 matched detections per row, but Naive used a different recorded renderer setup. The available LoKr checkpoint is step 10000; these historical measurements do not establish that checkpoint identity. No cohort means no measured likeness result, not zero likeness.

sections.title: A finite capture cannot span every input direction
sections.body: The selected historical repair stored 1024 class rows and 1024 trigger rows per layer. Their combined matrix has rank at most 2048, so its nullspace has at least input width minus 2048 dimensions. For a vector absent from both captures, zero-centered ridge gives A-prime v = 0 in exact arithmetic; a source-centered prior gives A-prime v = A v. These are algebraic coverage bounds, not measured ranks or semantic labels. They do not show that the omitted directions carried useful identity information or caused a particular scene failure; finite-precision outputs are also approximate.

sections.title: Excellent local fit did not certify preserved behavior
sections.body: These are median activation-response diagnostics across 256 edited layers for the selected scalar repair. Full BA responses are measured on fixed captured inputs. The held-out column uses a fresh token draw from the same prompt setup, so it is only a sampling holdout. The fitting gap is substantial even under that weak test. Response ratios and cosines are not face scores, and this aggregate does not identify which layers cause a rendered failure.

sections.title: A preservation method and a repair need not compose cleanly
sections.body: In this tested composition, applying surgery to DOP increased generic raw similarity and the scene-vocabulary median. Final-output preservation can coexist with nonzero intermediate activity, so suppressing local responses may disturb a useful computation. That explanation remains a hypothesis. Equal detection counts do not establish identical detected subsets, and this result does not cover every possible DOP-aware repair.

sections.title: Unrelated controls measure a different preservation requirement
sections.body: The recorded instrument is facebook/dinov2-base. Each image is processed with its AutoImageProcessor; the final-layer CLS token is normalized to unit length. The reported distance is 1 minus the dot product of the generated-image and matched-base embeddings: 1 minus cosine similarity. Images are converted to RGB with EXIF orientation applied. A larger distance means a larger representation change, not a calibrated amount of visual damage. Keep the three control families separate. Low target-face similarity alone cannot establish scene fidelity, requested-attribute adherence or preservation of unrelated capabilities.

sections.title: How to use these numbers in a new experiment
sections.body: Treat these aggregates as case studies that suggest controls: preserve both trigger states, pair the exact prompt and seed with its base, inspect detector misses, compare matching cases, repeat capture draws, and reserve unseen prompts before choosing settings. A broad archive from one character is not evidence of transfer to other characters, adapters or base models. The displayed comparisons are a selection from this broader work.
